alloys.alloys_notes: Balance Fe; the reported composition (30.34% Mn, 8.93% Al, 0.9% C) applies to all samples; solution treatment eliminates the κ-carbide precipitates that are present in the as-hot-rolled S0 condition.
alloys.description: Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density austenitic steel prepared by vacuum melting, used to investigate grain-size effects on Al-rich oxide film formation and corrosion resistance; single-phase FCC austenite after solution treatment.

source.reason: b0019 reports the Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steel composition (including 30.34% Mn, 8.93% Al, and 0.9% C) prepared via vacuum melting, and this single composition is used for all S0/S950/S1050/S1150 samples; b0008 refers to the material as Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels.

paper.paper_scope: Investigates how grain size (8.7–32 μm), controlled by solution treatment temperature (950–1150 °C), affects the formation of Al-rich oxide films and the corrosion resistance of Fe-Mn-Al-C low-density steels (S0/S950/S1050/S1150).
paper.title: Enhancing the corrosion resistance of low-density steels via Al-rich oxide film formation by grain size optimization

processes.description: Steel ingot homogenized at 1200 °C for 2 h, hot rolled at 1200–950 °C into 20 mm-thick slabs, and water quenched; no subsequent solution treatment.
processes.process_name: Hot rolled + water quenched (no solution treatment)
processes.processes_notes: S0 retains uneven/deformed grains and κ-carbide precipitates and serves as the baseline condition before solution treatment.
